title: Clarence Williams's tunes in New York and the sidemen of his band
summary: He recalls Clarence Williams bringing him tunes at Healy's, his impeccable band's look, and sidemen like Meyer Weinberg, Joe Loyacano, Eddie Powers and Almerico.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: I mean I'm like Louis Armstrong and I'm a contemporary. I helped him when he had patches in his pants. I helped many a colored man. I remember, I know he published Don't Mean a Thing If You Ain't Got That Swing, because I played the first three of them, Clarence Williams. And when I went to New York to play at Healy's Balkanades, and he called me up and he said, Johnny I've got some new tunes and they just fit you, and if you don't mind I'll come to rehearsal and tell you how I think they should be played. Not that I want to teach you, but what I did, I heard about the tunes. So he brought Don't Mean a Thing and He Didn't Get That Swing. And there was another band that thought they were good. Well I was a featured band and they played while we rested, so you know, it was secondary. They didn't have the right instrumentation. They had a fiddle, a trumpet and a saxophone, the loudest I've heard of my life, and a toothless drummer. Well they didn't make the appearance. I was always for the stiff shirt tuxedo and the week time. My band was impeccable. I'll show you pictures, you'll see some nice looking fellas. But they could play. Like Meyer Weinberg, you remember Meyer Weinberg?
He calls himself Gene Meyer now.
I've never met him, I've heard him on the record.

Oh boy, he played the chorus, stay in your own backyard on the saxophone, and she'd go down for posterity. And I had Joseph Larkana who died not long ago, his name was Erasmus, but he called himself Joe, he didn't like the name Erasmus. He only had one lady.

At that time, he was with me, I'll show you the picture. And I had Eddie Powers who was in the man always on time. I had a fine band. I had Tony Almarico as my hot man. And Red Bowman as my first trumpet player. Wyatt Sharp as my trabumpa. He's not on the Jerry L.A. Do you know him?
He has a man in Jackson, Mississippi.
What is his name? Wyatt Sharp.
